name: stayapi/booking-com-review-scraper
what_it_holds: Small (2-commit) MIT-licensed client wrapping the third-party 'StayAPI' REST service to pull Booking.com guest reviews (guest name/country/traveler type, review title, positive/negative text, score, room type, nights stayed, dates, partner replies) and export to CSV/JSON (16-column flattened CSV shown in the README). Requires signing up for StayAPI (50 free test requests); not a self-contained scraper.
why_useful: Illustrates an available field schema (including 'nights stayed' per review) for Booking.com reviews, but is a thin wrapper around a paid third-party API rather than an independent data source or committed dataset.
license: MIT (wrapper code); underlying API is a commercial/paid service

name: Expedia Hotel Recommendations (Kaggle 2016)
what_it_holds: ~37M rows of Expedia search/click/booking logs (2013-2014), fields: user location, search destination, check-in/out dates, is_package, is_booking, hotel_cluster (100 clusters), hotel_country/market. Dozens of GitHub repos (mandalsubhajit/Kaggle--Expedia-Hotel-Recommendations, 26 stars; gouravshenoy/ExpediaHotelRecommendation, 7 stars; ~40 more found) contain only modeling notebooks — none redistribute the raw CSVs (Kaggle competition rules forbid it), so a Kaggle account/API key is required to pull the actual data. External host: kaggle.com/c/expedia-hotel-recommendations.
why_useful: Real Expedia booking-intent data with dates/destinations could inform seasonality/destination-mix patterns for gap 9 (competitor OTA volumes) and lead-time structure for gap 3 (RNPL), but the data is stale (2013-14), pre-dates current STR competitive dynamics, and requires manual Kaggle download — GitHub itself holds no data, only unusable duplicate solution code.
license: mixed (repos mostly no license; underlying Kaggle data has competition-specific terms)
size_hint: ~37M interaction rows in original Kaggle files; GitHub repos themselves are code-only (few KB)
last_activity: most recently updated fork 2025-12-03 (mandalsubhajit); original competition data unchanged since 2015
themes: Expedia and Hotels.com datasets (Expedia hotel recommendation Kaggle, personalized ranking ICDM 2013, Expedia scrapers), Trivago RecSys 2019, Kayak/Skyscanner scrapers
why_all: Real Expedia booking-intent data with dates/destinations could inform seasonality/destination-mix patterns for gap 9 (competitor OTA volumes) and lead-time structure for gap 3 (RNPL), but the data is stale (2013-14), pre-dates current STR competitive dynamics, and requires manual Kaggle download — GitHub itself holds no data, only unusable duplicate solution code.

name: Personalize Expedia Hotel Searches - ICDM 2013
what_it_holds: ICDM 2013 Data Mining Cup Expedia dataset: hotel search impression logs with property price, star rating, review score, location score, promotion flag, and click/booking labels, ~10M search-result rows across ~1000 destinations. Repos found (igorpejic/personalize_expedia_hotel_searches_2013, 7 stars — code-only, requires user-supplied train.csv/test.csv path; gxanth/Learning-to-rank-with-Expedia, MIT; jlin-vt/expedia2013; 5 more near-duplicate solution repos) hold only ranking-model code (LightGBM/XGBoost learning-to-rank scripts), not the raw data.
why_useful: If ever obtained, gives granular hotel price/rating/promo fields that could sanity-check OTA pricing-competition dynamics (gap 9) and search-to-book funnel structure analogous to Airbnb's; but again 2013-vintage, Kaggle-gated, and no GitHub mirror actually carries the CSVs.
